pages.title: Engineering & Design
pages.text: Home › The Tower Design & Engineering THE TOWER DESIGN AND ENGINEERING The Structure Is The Form This early engineering sketch reveals how the tower’s distinctive form was shaped through structure. The lines trace the changing geometry of the building as it rises, showing how architecture and engineering were developed together to turn a complex concept into a buildable structure Not a single office in the building faces south. A single formal act, subtracting a spiralling quadrant from a prismatic volume, created both the architectural identity and the structural system of Kuwait's most ambitious building THE ENGINEERING FEAT The Lamella At the foot of the tower, where the south wall begins its turn, the building opens into a lobby 24 metres high with not a single column standing in it. What holds it up is the lamella: a lattice of concrete members that gathers the weight of the tower above and carries it down to the ground around the edges of the space Five element types interlock to form the web, each shaped to the load it carries. The result is 900 square metres of open floor at the base of an eighty storey building, a space most towers would fill with columns and Al Hamra leaves clear Technical Specification The numbers behind the form Height Height to tip 412.6 m Occupied height 371.4 m Top floor height 368 m Sky Lounge elevation 351 m Structure RC shear wall core with perimeter MRF Foundation 289 piles at 1,200 mm diameter Pile depth range 22 to 27 m Raft thickness 4.0 m Structural steel 6,000 tons Reinforcing steel 38,000 tons Facade South wall limestone 258,000 m² (world Wide record) Curtain wall glass 55,000 m² Glass type Insulated low emissivity coating Curved glass units ~30% of total glass area Stone type (lower) Jura limestone tiles Stone type (upper) Trencadis (mesh + crushed limestone) Engineering Team Client Representative Ajial Real Estate & Entertainment Co. pages.title: Sustainability
pages.text: Home › The Tower Sustainability Environmental philosophy The form is the strategy In most buildings, sustainability arrives after the architecture is resolved, in the shape of solar panels, shading devices and green roofs. At Al Hamra Tower the environmental response generated the architecture. The spiralling form that makes the building unmistakable is the same act that removes the south facing glass, and the stone wall that defines the skyline is also the primary solar shield SOM's structural engineers describe the process as symbiotic evolution. The structural system and the exterior form developed together, and neither could exist without the other ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE 01 The Desert Wall The solid south wall, 258,000 square metres of Jura limestone, is the building's primary environmental strategy. Its geometry answers Kuwait's solar path directly. Openings are positioned according to the envelope's relationship to the sun at each floor level, so direct solar radiation never enters an office Zero south-facing offices, tower-wide 02 The Spiralling Form Removing a quarter of each floor plate on the south side does two things at once. It opens Gulf views to every tenant and it reduces the total surface exposed to desert sun. SOM calls it a purely formal operation, with architecture and environmental engineering solved by the same geometric act 30% less south facing surface than a conventional tower of equal area 03 Low E Insulating Glass 55,000 square metres of curtain wall on the north, east and west facades use insulating glass with a low emissivity coating. Roughly 30% of the units are curved to wrap the tower's corners, with the bending and coating processes designed to work in tandem 55,000 m² insulating curtain wall 04 Trencadis, Weight Reduced Stone The upper floors of the limestone cladding use trencadis, a mesh coated with crushed limestone, in place of full tiles. It cuts facade weight substantially at height while holding the visual continuity of the monolithic stone wall. A material innovation driven by structural necessity Significant weight reduction at height — same visual appearance 05 Smart Building Infrastructure A fibre optic backbone and an advanced building automation system, managed by a world leading facility management company, monitor and control every building system on every floor 100% power supply redundancy across 5 substations Leasing Inquiry → 06 Concrete Over Steel Al Hamra is one of the few reinforced concrete supertall buildings, a choice with long term sustainability implications. Concrete's thermal mass moderates internal temperature swings and its compressive strength allows efficient use of material. The 289 piles were designed for the chemistry of Kuwait's silty sand geology, to resist sulphate attack without corrosion 195,000 m³ reinforced concrete — structural longevity by design The solid south wall, and flared geometry, is generated in order to decrease the absorption of solar radiation. This wall not only protects the building from critical environmental conditions, it also assumes the role of structural backbone Skidmore, Owings & Merrill LLP — Structural Sustainability Statement

pages.text: Home › Privacy Policy Privacy Policy Effective Date · January 2026 This policy was last reviewed and updated on January 2026. This Privacy Policy describes how Al Hamra Tower ("we," "us," or "our") collects, uses, and protects the personal information of visitors to our website and of individuals who contact us. By using our website or submitting information through our forms, you acknowledge that you have read and understood this Privacy Policy. 01 Information we collect We collect information that you voluntarily provide when you contact us through our inquiry form, subscribe to updates, or request information about leasing opportunities. This typically includes your name, email address, telephone number, company name, and the details of your enquiry. We also automatically collect certain technical information when you visit our website, including your IP address, browser type, device identifier, pages visited, time spent on pages, and referring URLs. This information is collected through cookies and similar technologies. 02 How we use your information We use the information you provide to respond to your enquiries, to provide the services you have requested, to communicate with you about leasing opportunities or related matters, and to improve our website and services. We may also use your information to send you periodic communications about Al Hamra Tower, provided you have consented to receive such communications. You may opt out of these communications at any time. 03 Legal basis for processing Where applicable law requires a legal basis for processing your personal data, we rely on the following bases: your consent, the performance of a contract to which you are a party, compliance with a legal obligation to which we are subject, or the legitimate interests pursued by us or by a third party, except where such interests are overridden by your rights. 04 Sharing of information We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal information to third parties. We may share your information with trusted service providers who assist us in operating our website, conducting our business, or servicing you, provided that those parties agree to keep this information confidential. We may also disclose your information where required by law, in response to valid legal process, or to protect the rights, property, or safety of our organisation, our tenants, or others. 05 Cookies and tracking technologies Our website uses cookies and similar tracking technologies to distinguish you from other users, remember your preferences, and analyse how our website is used. This helps us provide you with a better experience and improve our services over time. You can set your browser to refuse all or some browser cookies, or to alert you when websites set or access cookies. If you disable or refuse cookies, please note that some parts of this website may become inaccessible or not function properly. 06 Data retention We will retain your personal information only for as long as is necessary for the purposes set out in this Privacy Policy, or for as long as we are required to retain it to comply with applicable legal, accounting, or reporting requirements. 07 Security We implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect your personal information against unauthorised access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction. However, no method of transmission over the Internet or method of electronic storage is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security. 08 Your rights Depending on your jurisdiction, you may have certain rights regarding your personal information, including the right to access, correct, delete, or restrict the processing of your personal data, the right to data portability, and the right to object to processing. To exercise any of these rights, or if you have any questions about how we handle your personal information, please contact us using the details provided below. 09 Third-party links Our website may contain links to third-party websites. We are not responsible for the privacy practices or the content of such websites. We encourage you to read the privacy policies of any third-party websites you visit. 10 Changes to this policy We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time to reflect changes in our practices, technology, legal requirements, or other factors. We will post any changes on this page with an updated revision date. We encourage you to review this policy periodically. 11 Contact us If you have any questions, comments, or requests regarding this Privacy Policy or our privacy practices, please contact us via our inquiry form or at the address listed in the footer of our website.

Al Hamra is one of the few reinforced concrete supertall buildings, a choice with long term sustainability implications. Concrete's thermal mass moderates internal temperature swings and its compressive strength allows efficient use of material. The 289 piles were designed for the chemistry of Kuwait's silty sand geology, to resist sulphate attack without corrosion

Removing a quarter of each floor plate on the south side does two things at once. It opens Gulf views to every tenant and it reduces the total surface exposed to desert sun. SOM calls it a purely formal operation, with architecture and environmental engineering solved by the same geometric act

The upper floors of the limestone cladding use trencadis, a mesh coated with crushed limestone, in place of full tiles. It cuts facade weight substantially at height while holding the visual continuity of the monolithic stone wall. A material innovation driven by structural necessity
feature_cards.image_caption_en: Significant weight reduction at height, same visual appearance

feature_cards.body_en: The solid south wall, 258,000 square metres of Jura limestone, is the building's primary environmental strategy. Its geometry answers Kuwait's solar path directly. Openings are positioned according to the envelope's relationship to the sun at each floor level, so direct solar radiation never enters an office
feature_cards.image_caption_en: Zero south facing office tower wide

timeline_entries.body_en: The lamella is built, a web of 24 metre curved elements arching outward from the core, cast in fiberglass formwork fabricated directly from 3D parametric models. It opens a column free lobby of 900 square metres. Engineers run non linear buckling analyses on every member before it carries load

A mixed use complex with a 200 metre tower is designed by Al Jazera Consultants. Excavation begins and 289 cast in place bored piles are sunk 22 to 27 metres into Kuwait's silty sand. Once the pour starts, the foundation work cannot stop

Kuwait City Municipality raises the maximum allowable building height to 400 metres. The client group engages Skidmore, Owings and Merrill to design a landmark. SOM begins concept design with the contractor already working below

SOM subtracts a spiralling quadrant from a prismatic volume and rotates it at every level above. Two hyperbolic paraboloid walls appear, the flared ribbons. The geometry turns the building transparent toward the Gulf and solid toward the desert. Construction begins
Al Hamra Tower tops out at 412.6 metres, among the ten tallest buildings in the world at completion. 258,000 square metres of Jura limestone stand finished in Sharq. Kuwait City has a new landmark

Al Hamra's environmental performance was not engineered into the building after the form was set. It was the form itself — every design decision that gave the tower its identity also solved an environmental problem.
SOM's structural engineers describe the process as symbiotic evolution. The structural system and the exterior form developed together, and neither could exist without the other
Skidmore, Owings & Merrill LLP — Structural Sustainability Statement

The solid south wall, and flared geometry, is generated in order to decrease the absorption of solar radiation. This wall not only protects the building from critical environmental conditions, it also assumes the role of structural backbone

The Al Hamra Tower's geometry was generated by a single decisive act: subtracting a spiraling quadrant from a simple prismatic volume, then rotating it incrementally at each higher level. The result is two hyperbolic paraboloid walls — the iconic flared ribbons — that extend the full 412 metres of the building's height.

In most buildings, sustainability arrives after the architecture is resolved, in the shape of solar panels, shading devices and green roofs. At Al Hamra Tower the environmental response generated the architecture. The spiralling form that makes the building unmistakable is the same act that removes the south facing glass, and the stone wall that defines the skyline is also the primary solar shield
